observation: Fresh executor isolation did not eliminate the unsafe failure, falsifying executor accumulation as a sufficient cause. Control-lane routing allowed some supersession attempts to advance to cancellation, but the designated agent or unrelated healthy Activities still exhausted the five-second Bolt open timeout while all item processes shared one database file. Activity retry then exposed a second issue: unsafe supersession is not identity-stable after a partially completed attempt.
inference: The shared multi-process destination lock is the common upstream bottleneck. When a designated agent cannot reopen the store, it never reaches before-completion and cancellation waits forever; when a healthy Activity cannot open it, the arm fails directly. Control-queue capacity cannot repair destination-lock starvation. The unsafe identity change is inferred to be a downstream retry-idempotency defect triggered after an effect Activity exceeds its timeout.
falsifier: If extending the Bolt acquisition budget through the enclosing Activity/process deadline does not eliminate healthy-item open timeouts and allow the exact designated barriers to advance, shared-store lock starvation is not a sufficient diagnosis. If unsafe identity changes recur without a supersession retry, retry idempotency is not their cause.
correction: Retain the versioned control lane, extend the multi-process Bolt acquisition budget from five to thirty seconds while Temporal and experiment deadlines remain the outer bounds, restore a shared executor so repetition matches pilot lifecycle, then rerun the exact targeted cases. If unsafe identity drift remains, make supersession retry-idempotent without weakening its negative control.
